input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: The term runs Product-by-Product and country-by-country until the Secondary Royalty Terms expire (13.1), a multi-year committed term, yet Ono's only at-will exit (13.2) does not arise until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, and the notice figure is redacted. Ono therefore has no convenience exit throughout development and pre-launch and the notice cannot be verified against the 30-day preferred or 60-90 day fallback thresholds - walk-away territory under T4C. Our single edit to 13.2 makes the right exercisable for convenience at any time, fixes notice at thirty (30) days and adds a pro rata refund of fees prepaid for the post-termination period, retaining "for any reasons" and the rationale formality verbatim and leaving 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 untouched. The fourth preferred element is already met: Array's only exits are material breach (13.3), bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2); I have re-read 13.5, which grants termination rights to Ono alone (Safety Reasons and Efficacy Reasons), so Array has no at-will exit anywhere in Article 13 and no carve-out is needed. Raised separately, not in this redline: the Section 8.2 Competing Product tail keys a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term and can now bite earlier; and Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee is unaffected because the refund reaches only period-allocated prepayments.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
mappings.quote: 13.3 Termination for Material Breach. Either Party may terminate this Agreement in its entirety in the event the other Party shall have materially breached or defaulted in the performance of any of its material obligations hereunder
